notes: §1985:IV.4.4.2 GR3 requires three behaviours: "When any COBOL statement is executed which results in the execution of a declarative section, an implicit transfer of control to the declarative section occurs" (and back, per paragraph 1); ALTER "does not in itself constitute an explicit transfer of control, but affects the explicit transfer of control that occurs when the associated GO TO statement is executed"; and EXIT PROGRAM "causes an explicit transfer of control only when the statement is executed in a called program". DispatchEmitter.EmitUseMachinery emits __IoCheck, which after an unsuccessful I-O status selects the USE procedure and runs its pc range through __RunUse (EmitRunUseBody, a bounded __Dispatch call that returns to the statement after the I-O statement). AlterSwitchEmitter.EmitAlter only assigns the paragraph's _alter field and EmitGoTo transfers to that field's current value; the 1985 edition reaches it because VersionConformancePass.VisitAlterStatement (construct AlterRemoved2002) admits ALTER at --std 85 and SetAlterBinder.BindAlter binds it. CallEmitter.EmitExitProgram gates the return on __asCalled, so in a program that was not called control passes to the next statement. The witness runs all three (a USE AFTER ERROR declarative on an at-end READ, an ALTERed GO TO, EXIT PROGRAM in the main program); a probe added a re-ALTERed GO TO, ALTER state kept across CALLs, and EXIT PROGRAM returning from a called program.

next.reason: 1985 GR3 states the implicit transfer to a declarative section, the explicit-transfer rule, the ALTER sentence ('The execution of the procedure branching statement ALTER does not in itself constitute an explicit transfer of control, but affects ... the associated GO TO'), EXIT PROGRAM, and 'next executable statement' (§1985:IV.4.4.2 GR3). 2023 keeps the implicit transfer to exception processing procedures, 'An explicit transfer of control may be caused only by the execution of a procedure branching or conditional statement', the EXIT PROGRAM sentence and 'next executable statement' (§2023:14.6.3 GR3); the implicit performance of a USE BEFORE REPORTING declarative is stated by §2023:14.9.49.4 GR9. 2023 has no ALTER statement at all, so the ALTER sentence is gone and a 1985 program using ALTER is refused (stricter).
